subject: ela
skillName: Use technology to produce and publish writing
intro: This quiz checks how well you use technology to produce, publish, and share writing. You will choose the right digital tool for a purpose, pick formatting and editing features, write and respond to collaborative comments, credit sources, and follow safe online habits. Read each item carefully and choose the single best answer.

items.prompt:
Read the task: 'You need to send a polite, formal request to the school principal asking permission to start a recycling club.' Which digital tool fits this purpose best?
A) A formal email
B) A group text to your friends
C) A public blog post for the whole internet
D) A private journal app only you can read

steps: The purpose is to reach one specific reader, the principal, with a respectful, formal request.
A) A formal email is correct because email reaches one person directly and supports a polite, formal tone.
B) is wrong because a group text goes to friends, not the principal, and is too casual.
C) is wrong because a public blog post broadcasts to everyone instead of addressing the principal.
D) is wrong because a private journal is only seen by you, so the principal never receives the request.

items.prompt:
Read the goal: 'You want the three main sections of your report to stand out so readers can find them quickly.' Which word-processing feature best does this?
A) Adding a heading to each section
B) Changing the font color of every single word
C) Making the entire document italic
D) Making the page margins wider
items.answer: A) Adding a heading to each section

steps: The goal is to label and separate the sections so readers can scan and find them.
A) Adding a heading is correct because headings name and divide the sections clearly.
B) is wrong because coloring every word is decoration that does not organize the sections.
C) is wrong because italicizing the whole document changes appearance but does not mark sections.
D) is wrong because wider margins change spacing but do not help readers locate the sections.

items.prompt:
Read the scenario: 'You are about to publish your essay on the class blog.' Which choice shows safe, responsible online behavior?
A) Use a respectful tone and leave out private personal details
B) Include your home address and phone number in the post
C) Add an unkind comment about a classmate at the end
D) Share a friend's password so they can post too
items.answer: A) Use a respectful tone and leave out private personal details

steps: Safe publishing means protecting personal information and treating others with respect.
A) is correct because a respectful tone and keeping private details private keeps you and others safe.
B) is wrong because posting a home address and phone number shares private information publicly.
C) is wrong because an unkind comment about a classmate is disrespectful and harmful.
D) is wrong because sharing a password puts a friend's account at risk.

items.prompt:
A classmate shares a draft and asks for feedback. Read these four comments and choose the one that is specific, kind, and useful.
A) Your second paragraph is clear, but the third one needs an example to support the point.
B) This part is bad.
C) Great job, no changes needed.
D) Why did you even write this?
items.answer: A) Your second paragraph is clear, but the third one needs an example to support the point.

steps: Useful collaborative feedback points to a specific part, stays respectful, and suggests a concrete improvement.
A) is correct because it names a specific paragraph, gives a positive note, and suggests adding an example.
B) is wrong because 'This part is bad' is vague and unkind and gives no way to improve.
C) is wrong because 'Great job, no changes' is vague praise that does not help the writer revise.
D) is wrong because it is a harsh, off-topic remark, not feedback.

items.prompt:
Read the sentence from a draft: 'The principle of our school read the announcement to the sixth graders.' The spell checker shows no spelling errors. Which choice correctly fixes the real problem?
A) Change 'principle' to 'principal' because it names the head of a school
B) Leave it as is because spell check found no errors
C) Change 'read' to 'red' to match the spelling
D) Change 'announcement' to 'announcment'
items.answer: A) Change 'principle' to 'principal' because it names the head of a school

steps: Spell check accepts a correctly spelled word even when it is the wrong word for the meaning.
A) is correct because the head of a school is the 'principal', while 'principle' means a rule or belief.
B) is wrong because trusting spell check completely misses this real-word error.
C) is wrong because 'read' is the correct word here; 'red' is a color.
D) is wrong because 'announcment' is misspelled and 'announcement' was already correct.

items.prompt:
Read the situation: 'While researching your report, you found a helpful fact on a website and want to use it.' What is the responsible way to use it?
A) Put the fact in your own words and name the source
B) Copy the sentences word for word and do not mention the site
C) Change a few words and claim the idea as your own
D) Use it and say a friend told you the fact
items.answer: A) Put the fact in your own words and name the source

steps: Using online information responsibly means paraphrasing and crediting where it came from to avoid plagiarism.
A) is correct because putting the fact in your own words and naming the source gives proper credit.
B) is wrong because copying word for word with no credit is plagiarism.
C) is wrong because swapping a few words and claiming the idea is still plagiarism.
D) is wrong because a vague 'a friend told me' hides the real source and does not credit it.

items.prompt:
Two students are working on a shared document. One leaves this comment on a paragraph: 'Could you add a source for this statistic? It would make the point stronger.' Read the four possible replies and choose the response that best moves the writing forward.
A) Good point. I will add a link to the study where I found the number.
B) Delete the comment without replying and keep the draft the same.
C) Reply 'Stop telling me what to do' and move on.
D) Reply 'Whatever' and change a different paragraph that had no problem.
items.answer: A) Good point. I will add a link to the study where I found the number.

steps: A good response to feedback accepts a useful suggestion and states a clear next step that improves the writing.
A) is correct because it agrees with the on-topic suggestion and gives a concrete plan to add the source.
B) is wrong because deleting the comment and changing nothing ignores helpful feedback.
C) is wrong because it is a defensive, dismissive reply that does not improve the draft.
D) is wrong because it brushes off the comment and edits an unrelated paragraph instead of adding the source.

items.prompt:
A student is publishing a multi-page report online and wants it to look organized, be honest about its facts, and be safe to share. The report has three sections with no labels, includes a fact copied straight from a website, and ends with the student's full home address. Which set of changes best serves the reader and the writer?
A) Add a heading to each section, paraphrase the website fact and credit the source, and remove the home address
B) Make every word a different color, copy the fact exactly, and keep the home address so readers can visit
C) Italicize the whole report, claim the fact as original, and add a phone number too
D) Leave the sections unlabeled, change a few words in the fact, and post a classmate's address for fun
items.answer: A) Add a heading to each section, paraphrase the website fact and credit the source, and remove the home address

steps: The best choice fixes all three goals at once: organization, honest sourcing, and online safety.
A) is correct because headings organize the sections, paraphrasing and crediting avoids plagiarism, and removing the address protects personal information.
B) is wrong because coloring every word does not organize, copying the fact is plagiarism, and keeping the address is unsafe.
C) is wrong because italicizing everything does not label sections, claiming the fact is plagiarism, and adding a phone number shares private information.
D) is wrong because unlabeled sections stay disorganized, changing a few words is still plagiarism, and posting a classmate's address is unsafe and disrespectful.
